answer: To vote on where visitors may wander along a ridge to collect crystal, require a credential from a civil registry. The registrar checks identity against its person record and issues one credential ID per person; replacement keys retain that ID. Validators accept one ballot per credential ID in each election, across all accounts. Extra keys add no votes; another effective ballot needs another registered person willing to participate. Forged or duplicate registry records and bought votes remain possible, so this depends on registry integrity.
